neighbours: Ehrhart form (weaker): for every admissible triple there is a lattice polytope $Q$ with $\#(tQ\cap\mathbb{Z}^{\dim Q})=c^{t\nu}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$ for all $t\ge 1$.

Haase-McAllister form (weaker): $H(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is $\mathrm{GL}_{D}(\mathbb{Z})$-equidecomposable with a disjoint union of integral open simplices (Conjecture 3.2 of Haase and McAllister, restricted to hive polytopes); the pieces need not reassemble into one convex lattice polytope, which is why this form is weaker than the statement.

Rank restriction: the statement for partitions with at most $n$ parts. For $n\le 3$ the hive polytope has dimension at most one and is a lattice polytope (proved in the attempt of this record); for $n=4$ Buch states, without a printed proof, that every hive polytope has integral vertices, which would settle that case; from $n=5$ on hive polytopes with a vertex of denominator $2$ occur and the statement is open.
resolution_criteria: A proof establishes the existence of the decomposition $\{T_{i}\}$ and the maps $\{U_{i}\}$ for every admissible triple $(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$, by an explicit construction or by an existence argument; it may decompose $H$ into finitely many relatively open rational polytopes instead of simplices, since each such polytope is a finite disjoint union of relatively open rational simplices. A disproof exhibits one admissible triple for which no such decomposition exists. In particular, a triple whose polynomial $c^{t\nu}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$ is not the Ehrhart polynomial of any lattice polytope refutes the statement (for example through an inequality that the $h^{*}$-vector of every lattice polytope satisfies, or through Scott's inequality in dimension two), and so does any invariant of $\mathrm{GL}_{D}(\mathbb{Z})$-equidecomposability that separates $H$ from every lattice polytope. A proof or disproof restricted to a class of triples (a fixed number of parts $n$, full-dimensional hive polytopes, or a bounded size) resolves that class and not the statement; the case $n\le 3$, where every hive polytope has dimension at most one and is a lattice polytope, is settled in the affirmative; for $n=4$, Buch's statement that every hive polytope has integral vertices, which has no printed proof, would settle that case.
statement:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\lambda,\mu,
u$ be partitions with at most $n$ parts, $|\lambda|+|\mu|=|
u|$ and Littlewood-Richardson coefficient $c^{
u}_{\lambda\mu}>0$. Let $H=H(\lambda,\mu,
u)\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}$, $D= inom{n-1}{2}$, be the hive polytope of Knutson and Tao: the set of real labellings of the $D$ interior vertices of the triangular hive array of side $n$ whose border labels are $0$ at the apex and the partial sums of $\lambda$, $\mu$ and $
u$ along the three sides, and which satisfy every rhombus inequality (the sum of the labels at the two obtuse vertices of each unit rhombus is at least the sum at the two acute vertices). $H$ is a rational polytope whose lattice points are the integral hives, so that $\#(tH\cap\mathbb{Z}^{D})=c^{t
u}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$ for every integer $t\ge 1$.

Statement. For every such triple, $H(\lambda,\mu,
u)$ is $\mathrm{GL}_{D}(\mathbb{Z})$-equidecomposable with a lattice polytope: there exist finitely many relatively open rational simplices $T_{1},\dots,T_{r}$ with $H= igsqcup_{i=1}^{r}T_{i}$ (disjoint union, every face of the decomposition counted once as the relative interior of a simplex of some dimension between $0$ and $\dim H$) and affine unimodular maps $U_{i}(x)=A_{i}x+b_{i}$ with $A_{i}\in\mathrm{GL}_{D}(\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_{i}\in\mathbb{Z}^{D}$, such that the images $U_{1}(T_{1}),\dots,U_{r}(T_{r})$ are pairwise disjoint and $Q= igsqcup_{i=1}^{r}U_{i}(T_{i})$ is a lattice polytope, that is, a convex polytope all of whose vertices lie in $\mathbb{Z}^{D}$. In particular $\#(tH\cap\mathbb{Z}^{D})=\#(tQ\cap\mathbb{Z}^{D})$ for every $t\ge 1$, so the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial $c^{t
u}_{t\lambda,t\mu}$ is the Ehrhart polynomial of the lattice polytope $Q$.
title: Equidecomposability of hive polytopes with lattice polytopes
